sentences.text:
Suryanarayan Singh vs Superintendent Of Police on 11 March,
2025

In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
 Crlmc No. 4347 of 2024
 Suryanarayan Singh .... Petitioner(s)
 Mr. P.K. Sahoo, Advocate
 -versus-
 Superintendent of Police, Cbi, .... Opposite Party (s)
 Acb, Bhubaneswar.

entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Mr. Sarthak Nayak,
 Special P.P.
 Coram:
 Justice Sibo Sankar Mishra
 Order
Order No. 11.03.2025 01. 1. Heard.

2. The petitioner is aggrieved by the order dated 13.09.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge,
(CBI-I), Bhubaneswar, whereby the learned trial court after accepting the protest petition filed by the Petitioner, directed to proceed for inquiry under Section-202 of the Cr.P.C.
3.

Initially the F.I.R. was registered on 17.05.2021 against the unknown persons for the alleged commission of offences under Section 120-B/420 of I.P.C. read with Sections 13(2)/13(1)(d) of the P.C. Act.
After investigation, the CBI has filed closure report/final report on 03.12.2021.
4. The learned trial Court after hearing the Public Prosecutor and the informant, accepted the closure report and allowed the petitioner-informant to file the protest petition.
The protest petition was heard and thereafter the impugned order has been passed.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that on the earlier occasions, the petitioner being the informant had approached this Court by filing CRLMC No.2339 of 2022 challenging the order dated 22.07.2022 passed by the learned Special Judge, CBI-1, Bhubaneswar.

Relevant is to reproduce the said order:-
"7.

In case of a final report/closure report as in the present case by the CBI, a court does have couple of options either to accept the said report and invite a protest petition to treat it as complaint and proceed according to law or it may also direct further investigation by the investigating agency considering the materials on record or even on the same material collected during investigation take cognizance of the Suryanarayan Singh vs Superintendent Of Police on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104682415/
1 offence or on such protest petition received from the informant.

entities.text: Suryanarayan Singh vs Superintendent Of Police
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the instant case,
since there was a protest petition, hence petitioner should have been heard him vis--vis the closure report instead of registration of a complaint, the Court is of the view that such an opportunity should be provided to him with a liberty to file an application in respect thereof.
8. Accordingly, it is ordered.
9. In the result, CRLMC stands allowed.

Consequently, the impugned order dated 22nd July, 2022 passed in 1CC No.28 of 2022 by the learned Special Judge (CBI-1),
Bhubaneswar is hereby set aside.

As a necessary corollary, in view of the conclusion reached at, the petitioner is allowed with a liberty to move an application before the learned court below for hearing on the closure report submitted by the CBI and in the event, any such application so moved by him, the learned Special Judge (CBI-1),
Bhubaneswar shall consider the same and pass appropriate orders as per and in accordance with law."
6.

Relying upon the aforementioned observations made by the coordinate Bench by this Court while disposing the CRLMC No.2339 of 2022 filed by the Petitioner, learned Counsel for the Petitioner submits that before the impugned order could be passed, it was obligatory on the part of the learned trial Court to hear him out.

7. I have perused the impugned order dated 13.09.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge (CBI-I),
Bhubaneswar in I.C.C. Case No.28 of 2022 and the proceeding sheet of the learned trial Court in the case.
It appears that the Petitioner being the Informant has been extensively heard by the learned trial Court while entertaining his protest petition.

However, the issuance of the process against the accused persons has been deferred till the inquiry under Section-202 Cr.P.C. is concluded and also opportunity was afforded to the petitioner to lead his own evidence to establish the case in the protest/complaint filed by him.

Since the impugned order is well within the purview of law contemplated under Section-200 and 202 of the Cr.P.C. and option has been given to the Petitioner to lead his own evidence, I am of the considered view that there is no prejudice caused to the petitioner.
Hence, I am not inclined to entertain this petition at this stage.
8. Accordingly, the CRLMC is dismissed.

However, liberty is granted to the Petitioner to lead his evidence under in the enquiry process under Section-202 of the Cr.P.C.
9.
Needless to say that it is open for the Petitioner to lead any kind of evidence he desires to establish his case.

(S.S. Mishra) Judge Narayan Designation: Personal Assistant Suryanarayan Singh vs Superintendent Of Police on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104682415/
